headline: BNP MP Ferdousi Ahmed Misty resigns following PM's directive
summary: The resignation follows allegations of her involvement in attacks and vandalism at a health center in Mirpur, Dhaka.
details: BNP reserved seat MP Ferdousi Ahmed Misty submitted her resignation on Thursday following a directive from the party leadership and the Prime Minister.
The move comes after Misty's name was linked to attacks, looting, and vandalism at the Radda MCH-FP Health Center in Mirpur, Dhaka.
Attorney General Md. Ruhul Quddus Kajal stated that the Prime Minister's directive sends a clear message that no one will be spared if allegations of wrongdoing are found.
The Attorney General highlighted a contrast with Jamaat-e-Islami, which expelled MP Gazi Nazrul Islam from the party, but since he did not resign, his parliamentary seat remains vacant.
According to the Attorney General, the BNP's action demonstrates a commitment to discipline and accountability, ensuring that achievements are not tarnished by individual misconduct.
The Election Commission has stated that a by-poll for the now-vacant reserved seat must be held within 90 days.
caption:
A BNP MP has resigned after being linked to attacks on a health center. The Attorney General calls it a 'clear message' on accountability.

BNP reserved seat MP Ferdousi Ahmed Misty submitted her resignation on Thursday following a directive from the party leadership and the Prime Minister.

The move comes after Misty's name was linked to attacks, looting, and vandalism at the Radda MCH-FP Health Center in Mirpur, Dhaka.

Attorney General Md. Ruhul Quddus Kajal stated that the Prime Minister's directive sends a clear message that no one will be spared if allegations of wrongdoing are found.

The Attorney General highlighted a contrast with Jamaat-e-Islami, which expelled MP Gazi Nazrul Islam from the party, but since he did not resign, his parliamentary seat remains vacant.

According to the Attorney General, the BNP's action demonstrates a commitment to discipline and accountability, ensuring that achievements are not tarnished by individual misconduct.

The Election Commission has stated that a by-poll for the now-vacant reserved seat must be held within 90 days.

headline_marked: 11 staff [[sacked over Abu Sayed killing]] at Begum Rokeya University
headline: 11 staff sacked over Abu Sayed killing at Begum Rokeya University
summary: Three teachers and eight administrative staff were permanently dismissed following an order from the International Crimes Tribunal.
details: Begum Rokeya University has permanently dismissed 11 staff members, including three teachers, for their involvement in the killing of student Abu Sayed during the July 2024 Anti-discrimination Student Movement.
The decision was finalized during the university's 123rd syndicate meeting on Wednesday, acting on an order issued by the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT).
Abu Sayed, an English department student, was shot and killed by police outside the university gate on July 16, 2024, during protests demanding quota reform.
The dismissed teachers include Associate Prof Asaduzzaman Mandal Asad, Associate Prof Mashiur Rahman, and Associate Prof Shariful Islam, the former proctor.
Among the administrative staff sacked are former assistant registrars Rafiul Hasan Russell and Hafizur Rahman Tufan, and several other officers and security personnel.
Vice-Chancellor Prof Md Showkat Ali confirmed that the terminations were carried out after the ICT order was presented to the university syndicate.
The ICT-2 had previously handed down verdicts in a crimes against humanity case, sentencing two former police officers to death and others to varying prison terms.
caption:
11 university staff, including 3 teachers, have been sacked for their role in the killing of Abu Sayed.

Begum Rokeya University has permanently dismissed 11 staff members, including three teachers, for their involvement in the killing of student Abu Sayed during the July 2024 Anti-discrimination Student Movement.

The decision was finalized during the university's 123rd syndicate meeting on Wednesday, acting on an order issued by the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT).

Abu Sayed, an English department student, was shot and killed by police outside the university gate on July 16, 2024, during protests demanding quota reform.

The dismissed teachers include Associate Prof Asaduzzaman Mandal Asad, Associate Prof Mashiur Rahman, and Associate Prof Shariful Islam, the former proctor.

Among the administrative staff sacked are former assistant registrars Rafiul Hasan Russell and Hafizur Rahman Tufan, and several other officers and security personnel.

Vice-Chancellor Prof Md Showkat Ali confirmed that the terminations were carried out after the ICT order was presented to the university syndicate.

The ICT-2 had previously handed down verdicts in a crimes against humanity case, sentencing two former police officers to death and others to varying prison terms.
